# EDN Main State Machine Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

This module is the central control sequencer for the EDN’s CSRNG application-command flow. It decides when a command must be loaded, when a command must be sent, and when the EDN must wait for the CSRNG to acknowledge that a command has completed.

The module operates in three broad modes:

- **Boot-time request mode**  
  The module autonomously sequences a boot-time instantiate command followed by a generate command.

- **Auto request mode**  
  The module repeatedly dispatches generate and reseed commands, alternating between them according to the generate-request limit condition. The initial instantiate command is not generated by this module; it must be loaded by firmware through the software command path.

- **Software-port-only mode**  
  The module performs no hardware command generation. It is used when the EDN is enabled but neither boot-time nor auto request mode is selected.

The module shall be inactive and in its idle state after reset. It shall not issue any command-related strobes until it is enabled.

---

## 2. Reset and Idle Behavior

On reset, the module shall enter the idle state and all command strobes, status outputs, and error outputs shall be deasserted.

In the idle state, the module shall behave as follows:

- If the module is not enabled, it shall remain idle.
- If the module is enabled and boot-time request mode is selected, it shall start the boot-time request sequence.
- If the module is enabled and boot-time request mode is not selected but auto request mode is selected, it shall start the auto request sequence.
- If the module is enabled and neither boot-time nor auto request mode is selected, it shall emit a single completion pulse and enter a passive software-port-only state.

Boot-time request mode shall take priority over auto request mode when both are selected.

---

## 3. Software-Port-Only Mode

When the module enters software-port-only mode, it shall:

- Generate no hardware command requests.
- Emit no command-send, FIFO-capture, or interrupt-gate strobes.
- Remain in this mode until the global enable is deasserted.
- Return to idle when the global enable is deasserted.

A completion pulse is emitted on entry into this mode to indicate that no hardware-controlled command generation will occur.

---

## 4. Boot-Time Request Mode

When boot-time request mode is entered, the module shall perform the following sequence:

1. Assert the load-instantiate-command strobe so that the predefined boot-time instantiate command is loaded into the command path.
2. Assert the load-generate-command strobe so that the default generate command is loaded into the generate command FIFO.
3. Wait for the CSRNG to acknowledge the instantiate command.
4. After the instantiate acknowledgement is received, capture the current generate command FIFO count.
5. Assert the boot generate-command send strobe and hold it until the generate command has been sent.
6. Wait for the CSRNG to acknowledge completion of the generate command.
7. After the generate command acknowledgement is received, emit a completion pulse and enter the boot-done holding state.

While waiting for the instantiate or generate acknowledgement, the module shall remain in that waiting state until either:

- The CSRNG acknowledgement is received, or
- The global enable is deasserted.

If the global enable is deasserted before the sequence completes, the module shall return to idle. No completion pulse shall be emitted for an aborted boot sequence.

In the boot-done holding state, the module shall:

- Not issue any further commands.
- Keep the main busy status deasserted.
- Remain in that state until the global enable is deasserted.
- Return to idle when the global enable is deasserted.

---

## 5. Auto Request Mode

### 5.1 Entry and Initialization

When auto request mode is entered, the module shall not generate the instantiate command itself. Instead, it shall:

1. Assert an interrupt-gate strobe.
2. Assert the first-acknowledgement-wait status.
3. Wait for firmware to indicate that an instantiate command has been loaded through the software command request path.
4. After that load indication is received, wait for the CSRNG to acknowledge the instantiate command.
5. When the instantiate command is acknowledged, clear the interrupt-gate strobe and enter the auto dispatch loop.

If the global enable is deasserted during initialization, the module shall return to idle.

### 5.2 Dispatch Loop

At each dispatch decision point, the module shall evaluate:

- If the global enable is deasserted, return to idle.
- If auto request mode is no longer selected, emit a completion pulse and return to idle.
- If the number of generate requests remaining between reseeds is zero, select the reseed command path.
- Otherwise, select the generate command path.

The auto request mode busy status shall be asserted while the module is in the dispatch loop and while it is waiting for command acknowledgements in auto mode.

### 5.3 Generate Command Path

When the generate path is selected, the module shall:

1. Capture the current generate command FIFO count.
2. Assert the generate command send strobe and hold it until the generate command has been sent.
3. Wait for the CSRNG to acknowledge the generate command.
4. After acknowledgement, return to the dispatch decision point.

If the global enable is deasserted while waiting to send or while waiting for acknowledgement, the module shall return to idle.

### 5.4 Reseed Command Path

When the reseed path is selected, the module shall:

1. Capture the current reseed command FIFO count.
2. Assert the reseed command send strobe and hold it until the reseed command has been sent.
3. Wait for the CSRNG to acknowledge the reseed command.
4. After acknowledgement, return to the dispatch decision point.

If the global enable is deasserted while waiting to send or while waiting for acknowledgement, the module shall return to idle.

### 5.5 Exiting Auto Request Mode

Clearing auto request mode while a command is in progress shall not abort that command immediately. The module shall finish the current command and return to the dispatch decision point. At that point, because auto request mode is no longer selected, the module shall:

- Emit a completion pulse.
- Return to idle.

---

## 6. Completion Pulse Behavior

A completion pulse shall be emitted in the following situations:

- When the boot-time request sequence has finished its final generate command.
- When auto request mode is turned off and the module reaches the dispatch decision point with no further commands to issue.
- When the module is enabled with neither boot-time nor auto request mode selected.

The completion pulse shall be a single-cycle pulse and shall be deasserted at all other times.

---

## 7. Busy and Status Behavior

The module shall provide the following status behavior:

- A general busy status shall indicate that the module is actively sequencing a boot-time or auto request operation.
- The general busy status shall be deasserted in the idle state, in the boot-done holding state, during the boot completion pulse state, and in software-port-only mode.
- An auto-mode-specific busy status shall indicate that the auto request dispatch loop is active. This status shall be asserted after the initial instantiate command has been acknowledged and shall remain asserted until the auto mode loop terminates or the global enable is deasserted.
- The current operating state shall be exposed on a state observation output for status and debug. The state value shall update synchronously with the module clock.

---

## 8. Error Behavior

The module shall enter a terminal error state if:

- A local escalation/security alert condition is asserted in any state, or
- The current state is not one of the defined operating states.

When a local escalation is asserted, it shall take priority over all other state transitions and shall force the module into the error state on the next clock edge.

In the error state, the module shall:

- Assert the main error output continuously.
- Stop all command sequencing.
- Deassert all command-send strobes, FIFO-capture strobes, interrupt-gate strobes, and completion pulses.
- Remain in the error state until reset.

After reset, the module shall return to the idle state with all error status cleared.

---

## 9. Command Handshakes

The module distinguishes between sending a command and receiving a command acknowledgement:

- **Command sent** means the command has been transferred into the CSRNG command path.
- **Command acknowledged** means the CSRNG has completed processing of that command.

The module shall hold the relevant send strobe asserted until the command-sent condition is observed. The module shall not proceed to the next command until the corresponding acknowledgement condition is observed.

If the global enable is deasserted in the same cycle as a completion handshake, the disable condition shall take priority and the module shall return to idle.
